title: Best Monitor Arms UK
short: Monitor arms compared by adjustability, build quality and weight capacity, from budget single arms to heavy-duty dual mounts.
intro: A monitor arm frees up desk space and makes it far easier to get your screen at the right height and angle, but quality varies enormously with price. This guide compares arms hands-on tested by PCWorld, spanning budget picks to premium dual-monitor mounts.

products.name: LX Pro
products.best_for: Most people wanting an easy, high-quality single-arm setup
products.summary: PCWorld's top pick, with a wide clamp that spreads force safely across your desk and a genuinely tool-free setup thanks to a comfortable handhold clamp mechanism. Build quality feels competitive with far pricier arms, though its 22lb weight limit is slightly lower than its predecessor's.
pros: Wide clamp reduces desk damage risk
cons: Lower weight limit than the older Ergotron LX

products.name: MAG MT201
products.best_for: Buyers who want a sturdy arm without an Ergotron price
products.key_spec: Up to 49in / 44lbs rated, spring tension, quick-release VESA
products.summary: An inexpensive arm rated well beyond what most monitors need, with a quick-release VESA mount that's a nice touch at this price. PCWorld found the arm itself sturdy once built, though assembly is fiddly, taking 15-20 minutes with numerous awkwardly-placed screws.

products.name: HNSS6 Single Monitor Arm
products.best_for: Buyers who want the cheapest arm that still does the job properly
products.summary: PCWorld's go-to pick for the cheapest monitor arm worth buying. Setup needs just three screws, and the adjustable clamp spacing is more intuitive than rivals like the MountUp arm, though cable management covers are described as finicky and gas springs can lose tension over time.
pros: Very low price for a genuinely usable arm
cons: Gas spring tension can fade over time

products.name: Flo
products.best_for: Buyers who want the smoothest adjustment and best looks
products.summary: PCWorld found the Flo's operation the smoothest of any arm tested, adjustable with a mere nudge, with a refined VESA clip mount that handles recessed monitor mounts other arms struggle with. It's backed by a 12-year warranty and 24/7 support, though the price is steep for a single-monitor arm.
pros: Smoothest adjustment of any arm tested
Refined VESA mount handles recessed monitors well
cons: 20lb weight limit rules out some heavier monitors

products.name: HX
products.best_for: Buyers mounting a large ultrawide or heavy monitor
products.summary: A completely different, sturdier arm from the standard LX line rather than just an uprated version, easily handling both a 32in widescreen and 38in ultrawide in PCWorld's testing. Moving parts felt extremely smooth, though the height adjustment range is more limited than the LX and the design can feel bulky in a home office.
pros: Handles very large or heavy monitors with ease
cons: More limited height adjustment than the LX
Can look bulky in a home office

products.name: LX Dual (Side-by-Side)
products.best_for: Buyers who want two matched, high-quality arms on one mount
products.key_spec: Two arms rated up to 27in each, 10-year warranty
products.summary: Pairs two LX arms on a single mount, keeping the same winning build quality and smooth operation as the standalone LX Pro. Each arm is rated for monitors up to 27in side-by-side (smaller if stacked vertically), which is worth checking against your own screens before buying.
pros: Same build quality and smooth operation as the single LX
Supports both side-by-side and vertical arrangements
cons: 27in per-arm limit rules out larger monitor pairs
Costlier than buying budget dual arms

products.name: Workstream Dual Monitor Arm
products.best_for: Buyers who want two screens on arms without a premium price
products.key_spec: Roughly a quarter of the price of the Ergotron LX Dual
products.summary: PCWorld was impressed by the build quality on offer at around a quarter of the Ergotron LX Dual's price. It shares the same downsides as Monoprice's single-arm model: fiddlier to set up and less smooth in operation, and PCWorld was doubtful it fully lives up to its claimed 20lb-per-arm capacity.
pros: Impressive build quality for the price
Large saving over premium dual arms
cons: Real-world weight capacity likely below claimed spec

guide.q: Gas spring or spring tension arm?
guide.a: Gas spring arms tend to feel smoother and are common on premium arms, but the gas cylinder can lose potency over years of use. Mechanical spring-tension arms, like the MSI here, avoid that specific failure mode, though quality still varies a lot between models.

guide.q: How do I know if my monitor is compatible?
guide.a: Check your monitor supports a standard VESA mounting pattern (usually 75x75mm or 100x100mm) on the back, and confirm its weight falls comfortably within the arm's rated capacity, ideally well under the maximum rather than right at the limit.

guide.q: Is a heavy-duty arm worth it for a normal-sized monitor?
guide.a: Not usually. Heavy-duty arms like the Ergotron HX here are built for large ultrawide or 40-inch-plus monitors. A standard single-arm like the Ergotron LX Pro comfortably handles most 27-34in monitors at a lower price.

guide.q: Will a monitor arm damage my desk?
guide.a: A well-designed arm with a wide clamp, like the Ergotron picks here, spreads clamping force across more of your desk's edge, reducing the risk of marks or damage. Still, take care not to over-tighten any clamp, and check your desk's edge thickness is within the arm's supported range before buying.
